statement: The population $P(t)$ satisfies $\\dfrac{dP}{dt}=kP\\left(1-\\dfrac{P}{M}\\right)$ with $k,M>0$ and $P(0)=P_{0}$. Show that $P(t)=\\dfrac{M}{1+Ae^{-kt}}$ for some constant $A$, and express $A$ in terms of $P_{0}$ and $M$.
solution:
Separating variables, $\\frac{dP}{P(1-P/M)}=k\,dt$. Now $\\frac{1}{P(1-P/M)}=\\frac{M}{P(M-P)}=\\frac{1}{P}+\\frac{1}{M-P}$, so integrating gives $\\ln P-\\ln(M-P)=kt+C$, i.e. $\\frac{P}{M-P}=Ce^{kt}$. Solving for $P$: $P=\\frac{MCe^{kt}}{1+Ce^{kt}}=\\frac{M}{1+(1/C)e^{-kt}}=\\frac{M}{1+Ae^{-kt}}$ with $A=1/C$. At $t=0$, $P_{0}=\\frac{M}{1+A}$, so $A=\\frac{M-P_{0}}{P_{0}}$.
